messages:
maya: hitting a weird one with the async py client + Dedicated behind our proxy + custom CA. intermittent SSL failures, then the SDK starts hammering token refresh and we get a retry loop. anyone seen this pattern?

sam: can you paste the exact error and a minimal repro? async vs sync matters a lot here.

maya: yup -- small log dump. note this is Dedicated (private base_url) with company CA pinned via /etc/ssl/certs/company.pem and a forward proxy.

maya: ```
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain (_ssl.c:1123)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
httpx._exceptions.ProxyError: Error connecting to proxy at 10.0.0.5:3128 -- SSL transport error
...
2024-11-02T14:02:18Z maya redwood-python v0.12.0 async_client.post -> 502 from proxy on token refresh
2024-11-02T14:02:18Z maya retrying token refresh (attempt 3)
2024-11-02T14:02:19Z maya async task spawn -> duplicate request sent while refresh in-flight
```

jordan: this rings a bell. httpx async + httpcore proxy + custom CA sometimes needs an explicit SSLContext instead of just passing a path. which SDK param did you set? ca_bundle or ssl_context?

maya: I set REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/company.pem and also tried passing client=Auth(...) with verify=path for sync flow. async path uses httpx.AsyncClient under the hood so verify didn't always get wired through the proxy handshake.

sam: can you try setting trust_env=False and mount the proxy explicitly? also ensure the proxy process trusts the CA chain (often corp proxies re-sign). quick repro: 

sam: ```py
import ssl, httpx, os
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=os.environ['REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE'])
client = httpx.AsyncClient(proxies='http://10.0.0.5:3128', verify=ssl_ctx, trust_env=False, base_url='https://dedicated.customer.redwood.internal')
# use client for calls
```

lee: additional thing — our SDK's retry policy treats proxy 502/504 during token refresh as retriable and doesn't de-dupe concurrent refreshes, so multiple tasks try to refresh at once. that explains the hammer. we should serialize refreshes or use a lock.

maya: exactly. observed 10x token refreshes within seconds. when the proxy returned 502 for an upstream auth endpoint the SDK kept retrying with backoff but without jitter & without checking if a refresh is already running for the same token.

jordan: workaround: short-term you can set REDWOOD_RETRY_ON_AUTH_FAIL=false or bump REDWOOD_TOKEN_REFRESH_LOCK=true (if using internal env flags) — but those are internal flags. file a bug for public API.

maya: filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1423 (private repo link replaced) — titled "async: proxy+custom-ca triggers token refresh thundering + SSL handshake failures". included repro and logs.

sam: for the custom CA part we should also add docs showing how to provide an ssl.SSLContext to the AsyncClient via SDK options. right now only sync flow docs show verify=path.

lee: feature request: SDK should accept either ca_bundle path OR ssl_context (for async), and when running behind a proxy detect 5xx from proxy during token refresh and pause other refresh attempts until it either succeeds or a hard fail occurs. also better error surface: if VERIFY fails, add a hint about proxy re-signing and suggest trust_env=False + SSLContext.

maya: added repro sample in the issue with the snippet that sets ssl_context + trust_env=False. shared it with infra for proxy CA cert check.

infra-bot: note: staging-proxy cert rotation scheduled 2024-11-05 02:00 UTC. expect brief handshake failures.

jordan: one more thing — base_url parsing edge-case: if Dedicated base_url contains a trailing path (e.g., https://dedicated.customer.redwood.internal/prefix) our client builds auth URL as base_url + '/oauth/token' which can double up paths. watch for that when you pass base_url vs host.

maya: ugh that explains a lot for another customer. i'll include that in the issue too. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: tagging @devex for follow-up RFC to add ssl_context option and token-refresh lock.

lee: short checklist for folks hitting this: 1) try ssl.SSLContext(cafile=path) with AsyncClient verify, 2) trust_env=False, 3) ensure proxy trusts CA, 4) avoid putting path suffix in base_url, 5) watch SDK v0.12.1 release notes for token refresh fix.

maya: marking this resolved for my team after applying ssl_ctx + env change, still tracking upstream SDK fix in the GH issue.
